What their own code actually shows:
1. The crash game has no player seed. Provably fair normally means you add your own seed and results are computed from your seed plus theirs. In Gamdom's crash game the seed is one fixed constant hardcoded into the game file. It is the same for every player, every round, forever. Nothing about a round depends on you, and the house can know every upcoming result before anyone places a bet.
2. The crash formula carries a hidden house cut. The math in their code includes a term (a divide by 50) that is not part of the fair formula they describe publicly. There is also a built-in 1 in 100 chance that every round instantly crashes at 1.00x. Running their own formula, the real average return to players is about 97.8 percent, and it gets worse depending on where you cash out.
3. The payout rate is a live setting, not a fixed rule. Admins can change the house edge from a control panel, and the change even overrides the payout rate advertised by game providers. A game can be listed at one payout number and quietly repriced later.
4. For roulette and hilo, their own code comment admits the result mapping is "slightly biased because of modulo." They knew and wrote it down.
5. For dice, the player's seed is never saved to the database, so the "verify your result" feature cannot actually be used after the round.
6. The code also lets the system cut a crash round short and force-cash everyone out when total payouts hit a cap calculated from the live bets on the table.

TL;DR: The help page promises "the server seed is secret until reveal, nobody, the house included, can know your next result". Reality: the database stored the raw seed next to the hash, the crash game shipped with a fixed public seed so the house could see every result in advance, and the house edge was a runtime dial. That is not provably fair. That is trust-me with extra steps.

The live crash game file at gamdom.com/build/Crash.route.BBLHNSNC.js contains the fixed seed and the formula. Download it and read it yourself.
